To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RMT + SPE is more accurate than SPE alone, but that NMG shows that RMT + SPT is more accurate than SPT alone.
RMT+SPE outperforms RMT, but that NMG is more suitable than NIST score for evaluating RMT+SPE.

RMT+SPE and RMT are better than RMT alone in terms of NMG and NIST score, respectively, and the difference in the evaluation results between RMT+SPE (with NMG) and RMT (with NIST) is due to the fact that RMT+SME uses the reference corpus for the evaluation while RMT uses the reference translation only.

how to combine rule based machine translation with statistical post editor and how to measure the translation quality.
the evaluation of the translation quality and the combination of the rule based method and the statistical method.
a new evaluation measure for MT and the combination of a statistical based post-editor and a rule based machine translator.

RMT+SPE has better accuracy than RMT but it has some strange expressions in the outputs.
RMT+SPE and RMT are complementary to each other.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RMT+SPE method is more accurate but the RMT method is more fluent in the target language.
the combination of RMT and SPE is better for patent translation than RMT only and that the evaluation measure NMG is better than NIST for evaluating the translation quality of long sentences.

we should use a new evaluation method for patent translation.
the evaluation of MT should be based not only the accuracy but also the naturalness.
